subject: Autoscaler starvation during scheduled surge — remediation & credits
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Park <anna@lumenai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [Incident] Autoscaler starvation during scheduled surge — immediate update

Hi Anna,

Quick update: at ~08:42 PST our monitoring detected that your Dedicated pool experienced a sustained failure to scale for ~18 minutes during a planned marketing surge window. During that interval, a subset of model requests received elevated latency errors (5xx and timeouts). We believe the impact affected 4 endpoints in your reservation; traffic dropped by ~22% due to request-level retries and throttling.

Immediate actions we took:
- Put a temporary mitigation in place: increased reserved warm standbys for your pool to 20% above baseline (completed at 09:01 PST).
- Manually triggered a fallback routing policy to an alternative capacity tier for priority routes.
- Opened this thread to keep your team informed and copied our ops and account leads.

Next steps while we investigate:
1) We are collecting full request traces and autoscaler controller logs.
2) An interim postmortem with remediation will be shared by EOD (PST).
3) We will propose a tailored credit for the window of impact and any SLA thresholds affected.

Attachments: incident-starter-log-stub.txt (log excerpt)

I know this is disruptive—apologies. I will send a detailed follow-up with root cause and concrete mitigations shortly.

- Rafael
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: [Postmortem] Autoscaler starvation during scheduled surge — findings & remediation (redwood-postmortem-lumenai-20261125.pdf)

Anna — following up with initial findings and actions. The attached detailed postmortem contains logs, timeline, and action items; highlights below.

Summary of root cause (short):
- During your scheduled surge at 08:30 PST, the autoscaler warmup controller entered a fast-path that incorrectly reconciled pending scale-up requests when concurrent node-health updates arrived. A race condition in the warmup controller's allocation loop caused 16/18 scale-up requests to be dropped in-memory for a ~12–18 minute window. Because the fallback "burst-provision" policy relies on that same in-memory token, it did not trigger.

Why this manifested for LumenAI specifically:
- Your surge window aligned with a rolling maintenance job in the regional allocation service; that job caused repeated short-lived node health flaps which amplified the race.
- Your pool's prior warm-standby setting was at the lower bound (5%), which reduced available headroom when the race occurred.

What we did (actions completed):
- Immediately increased warm-standby to 20% and manually provisioned 6 burst nodes to stabilize traffic (09:01 PST).
- Applied an emergency hotfix to the warmup controller to serialize allocation updates (deployed 13:45 PST to canary, 14:05 PST to region).
- Triggered a one-time reroute for priority endpoints for your account for the remainder of the surge window.

Planned permanent mitigations:
- Correct the race in the warmup controller and add stronger unit/integration tests to prevent regressions (patch in PR, rollback-safe).
- Add a safety-path that will trigger cross-region proxy routing if local allocation fails for >10s.
- Change default customer warm-standby to 15% for accounts with predictable surge windows; we'll make this configurable for you.

Compensation proposal:
- We recommend a bill credit covering the affected window equivalent to 5% of your November committed usage, subject to your approval. If you prefer a fixed-dollar credit instead, we can propose $18,000 for the incident window (calculation attached in action items CSV).

Attachments in this message:
- redwood-postmortem-lumenai-20261125.pdf (full timeline, logs, mitigations)
- lumenai-action-items-20261125.csv (mapped owners & ETA)

I will be available on a call if you'd like to walk through the postmortem — proposing 10:30 PST tomorrow. Please let me know a time that works.

Regards,
Rafael
